name: THE HOME CENTER
rule: VAMILY rules 416 (the big interiors: the tile stays a house), 461, 451(a) (its ceiling at 10%), 59 (every tile its cost and its effect), 428 (roofs and cover), 441; ask row 468's list, the twelfth: 'THE HOME CENTER (WORLD TEN's new place), THE HOSPITAL, THE PRISON's cell blocks: smaller, still house-tiled.'
facts: A big home-improvement store is about 105,000 square feet under its roof with about 24,000 more of garden centre (Home Depot's own average, its annual report): about 68 fight tiles inside and 15 outside, so the board is the store, the lumber along its back wall and the garden yard at its side.

The racks are steel pallet racking twice a man's height with stock above, in rows with an aisle between: here a rack is a tile you cannot stand on, and a row of them is a wall with gaps at the main aisles.

In the collapse a home centre is the most useful building in a town: lumber, fasteners, tools, wire, propane, seed. What is left is what nobody could carry: the heavy racks, the lumber nobody needed, the checkout lanes.
The garden centre has no roof but its shade cloth: by day the light falls on the whole yard.
how_to_mod: A layout is 15 strings of 20 characters; every character is in 'legend'; every tile kind a legend entry names has its row in 'tiles' (its cost and its effect). A piece names the finished piece it is drawn as ('like') until this folder has its own art file (homecenter_art.json: floor lists and a kit, the garage's format). slices/bohemia_big_inside.js lays it; slices/fight_ground/insides.json lists the insides.
districts_why: The home centre is its own map kind and this board is all of it: the store, the lumber along its back wall and the garden yard at its side. So every fight at its cell is fought on it. (Measured: at seven in ten, the alpha's valley never dealt it: both its home centre cells rolled the lot.)
tiles_how: Rule 59: every kind of tile says what it costs to step on and what it does. 'row' is the fight's own ground row (flat 2 AP, rough 3, height +1 a level, obstacles none); 'open' is open floor (on AUTO nobody stays on it); 'good' is ground AUTO goes to; 'say' is the one line he reads when he taps it (draft, the fewest words). [bb] each kind is a Battle Brothers ground: flat, rough, an obstacle, and cover as its trees and walls give it.

wall.effect: The store's tilt-up wall, or the garden yard's fence: no way through.

floor.effect: The sales floor: sealed concrete, open ground, nothing to hide behind; on AUTO nobody stays on it.

gate.effect: A gap in the garden yard's fence: open ground, one way between the store and the yard.

rack.effect: Steel racking twice a man's height, what nobody could carry still on it: nobody stands on its tile; cover for the tiles beside it. [bb] its forest: a row of them is a wall with gaps.

lumber.effect: Lumber still banded in its bunks along the back wall: cover.

cart.effect: Flatbed carts, one tipped: low cover.

endcap.effect: An end cap at the end of a run of racks, its display knocked flat: low cover, and the way through the row.

stock.effect: A pallet of stock pulled down into the aisle and left: cover.

spill.effect: A rack's load spilled across the aisle: low cover, and slow going over it (3 AP). [bb] its brush.
spill.say: A spilled rack: low cover, slow going.

fallen.effect: Where a whole run of racking came down and was picked clean: open ground and slow going (3 AP a step). [bb] its rough ground.
fallen.say: Fallen racking: slow going, open ground.

checkout.effect: A checkout lane, its counter and its belt: low cover.

propane.effect: The propane exchange cage, its tanks long gone: cover.

rental.effect: The tool rental counter, a mixer and a lift left behind: cover.

plants.effect: Benches of dead plants in their pots: low cover, under the sky.
plants.say: Dead plants on benches: low cover.
plants.say_lit: Dead plants on benches: low cover, and the day is on you.

bags.effect: Soil and gravel bags stacked on pallets: cover, under the sky.
bags.say_lit: Stacked bags: cover, and the day is on you.

yard.effect: The garden yard: open ground under the shade cloth's rags; by day a man here is seen.
yard.say_lit: The garden yard: open ground, and the day is on you.

fire.effect: A fire in a drum somebody keeps. It burns day and night: a man in its light is seen.
fire.say_lit: A drum fire: you stand in its light, and they see you.

doors.effect: The store's doors, the glass gone: open ground, and by day the light falls in: a man here is seen.
doors.say_lit: The doors: open ground, and the day is on you.

kit_how: Every piece is drawn AS a finished piece of another kit ('like') until COOK's own picture for it is in homecenter_art.json under the same name: then that picture is used and nothing here changes. 'kind' is what it does in the fight (COVER, LOW_COVER, WALL); 'blocks_move' means nobody stands on its tile. A DRESS piece is drawn and never counted.
start_why: NO HIGH GROUND: a home centre is one floor. The racks are the board: rows of them with gaps, so a line breaks into duels at the main aisles.

ceiling.how: VAMILY rule 451(a): the store's roof, a warehouse roof (the corrugated deck, open-web joists, the strip lights most of them dead, a few clear panels), over the board at this alpha (10%, never past the fight's own most). 'src' is the picture COOK makes; 'have' true the day it is in the folder. Until then the fight draws 'kind' itself, a stand-in (the warehouse's).
